 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE CHANDRA SHEKHAR JHA
ORAL ORDER 4 08-01-2025 Heard the parties.

2. The present matter was taken on board for considering the prayer of bail and suspension of sentence of above named accused/appellant during pendency of appeal under Section 389(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure (in short Cr.P.C.) as raised through memo of appeal itself, which preferred under Sections 374(2) of the Cr.P.C.
3.

This application has been filed by the convict/appellant against the judgment of conviction dated 01.02.2024 and order of sentence dated 03.02.2024 rendered by learned ADJ VI cum Special Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.1226 of 2024(4) dt.08-01-2025 Judge, POCSO, Purnea in Purnia Sadar P.S. Case No. 341 of 2020 by which the learned trial court has convicted the appellant for the offences punishable under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code where ld. trial court sentenced the appellant to undergo rigorous imprisonment for ten years and fine of Rs. 25,000/-(Rupees Twenty five thousand) and in default of payment of fine he shall further undergo simple imprisonment for six months for the offence.

The period undergone shall be set-off under Section 428 of the Cr.P.C.
4.
Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant/convict submitted that the most important witness of present occurrence is victim herself who is examined as PW-1 during the trial.

It is pointed out from the statement of victim as recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C. and her Md. Majid vs The State Of Bihar on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141771035/
1 testimony as available through her depositions being PW-1, that allegation traveled from "rape" to "gang rape" making allegation prima-facie false on its face.

sentences.text: It is submitted that while recording statement Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.1226 of 2024(4) dt.08-01-2025 under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C., it was stated by vicitm that her mouth was pressed by the appellant whereas being PW-1 she deposed that her mouth was pressed by co-accused Md. Qudus.

It is further pointed out that from same statement it appears that rape was committed inside the vehicle but from her depositions being PW-1 it appears that rape was committed by this appellant/petitioner along with co-accused Md. Qudus somewhere else after kidnapping the victim.

It is pointed out that aforesaid major contradictions was completely ignored by learned trial court and as such judgment of convictions recorded by learned trial court believing victim as a "sterling witness" completely appears questionable on its face.

5. It is further submitted by learned counsel that even the doctor who examined the victim testified during the trial as PW-6, nowhere find any injury in or around private part of the victim suggesting prima-facie allegation of rape/gang rape false on its face.
It is Patna High Court CR.

APP (SJ)
No.1226 of 2024(4) dt.08-01-2025 submitted that upon cross-examination PW-6 doctor categorically testified during trial that victim didn't disclosed to him that rape was committed upon her.

6. Considering the nature of evidence as available out of depositions of prosecution witnesses particularly of PW-1/victim, it is submitted that balance of appeal is in favour of appellant/convict,
wherein he remains in custody for about four years and two months against fixed term sentence of ten year where this appeal is of March, 2024 itself and same is not likely to be taken up on board in near future for final hearing, therefore, on this score alone appellant/convict deserves bail.
7.

In support of his submissions learned counsel relied upon the legal report of Hon'ble Supreme Court as available through Atul @ Ashutosh vs. State of Madhya Pradesh reported in 2024 (3) SCC 663.
8.

sentences.text: Learned APP while opposing the prayer of bail and suspension of sentence submitted that victim categorically testified against appellant as to commit rape Patna High Court CR.
APP (SJ) No.1226 of 2024(4) dt.08-01-2025 upon her being PW-1 but he could not disputed the factual submission as advanced by learned counsel for the appellant.

9. In view of aforesaid factual submission and by taking note of major contradictions as surfaced during the trial out of statement of victim recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C. and her depositions being PW-1, coupled with the fact as appellant/convict remains in custody for about four year and two months, against the sentence of ten years, where this appeal is not likely to be taken up on board for final hearing in near future, as same is of March, 2024 itself, accordingly,
above named accused/appellant is directed to be released on bail, during the pendency of the appeal, furnishing bail bond of Rs. 10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned ADJ VI cum Special Judge, POCSO, Purnea in Purnia Sadar P.S. Case No. 341 of 2020.
